candidate.title: 3'-Seq
candidate.scope: The single 3′-Seq library-preparation schematic assigned to the Illumina 3′-Seq card, clarified by Lianoglou et al. (2013), Figure 1A and the full-text 3′-Seq protocol. One bead-associated poly(A)-junction route runs through first- and second-strand cDNA synthesis, U-directed nicking, nick translation and blunting to PCR-purified terminal cDNA. The second-adapter ligation interface is supplied by the caption and text, not a separate drawn panel. No alternative workflow is depicted. Sequencing-based isoform interpretation is readout context, beyond the image endpoint. The target labels 3′-Seq/3′-seq are typographic variants of this method, not distinct assays.

states.label: Poly(A)-tailed RNA annealed to a bead-bound, U-containing oligo(dT)-VN primer
features: The biological target is the 3′ end of polyadenylated RNA, including alternative 3′ UTR endpoints; total RNA is the reported starting sample.
The primer has a 3′ VN anchor, internal ribouridine, a sequencing-adapter sequence and a 5′ biotin attachment to streptavidin-coated magnetic beads.
The drawing writes the primer from left to right as NVTTTUTT(T)n and highlights U in red; the paper writes the primer sequence in the opposite, 5′-to-3′ orientation.

The catalogue calls the primer-borne sequencing-adapter sequence P5; the primary caption calls it the sequencing adapter at the primer’s 5′ end. Adapter interfaces are described here by position, using the primary caption’s terminology.

states.label: PCR-amplified, purified double-stranded 3′-end cDNA library
features: The drawing ends with a blue line labelled cDNA and no bead icon; the catalogue explicitly identifies the amplified product as double-stranded cDNA.

Sequenced cDNA end tags carry transcript-derived sequence adjacent to poly(A) sites; mapped tags identify 3′ endpoints and support relative 3′ UTR isoform abundance. These are RNA-abundance and endpoint-use readouts; protein expression is not directly measured.
The paper reports internal-priming-derived peaks that require removal, so oligo(dT)-VN priming does not ensure that every library fragment marks a genuine poly(A) cleavage site.
Sequencing and read analysis are readout context from the paper, beyond the displayed library-preparation endpoint.

method_scopes.rationale: All six depicted transformation captions belong to the card’s sole target, 3′-Seq. The unlabelled adapter-ligation interface is explicitly established for that same method in the primary caption and methods. The candidate RNA collection page is a verified secondary match: its heading names 3′-Seq and its caption and operation labels reproduce the assigned route. Its reviews, application references and associated kit names do not create additional target methods. Page 17 also lists Berkovits and Mayr (2015), Alternative 3′ UTRs act as scaffolds to regulate membrane protein localization, as a 3′-Seq application. Only the secondary citation and application description were inspected; no publication or metadata source for that article is supplied, so its implementation is not independently verified and it supplies no additional workflow target or chemistry.
